full_judgment:
2. Civil Appeal No.128 of 2009 has arisen from a Judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.31 of 2008. The High Court Division quashed the proceedings pursuant to a writ petition filed by the respondent Tasmima Hossain. The case arose out of ACC GR Case No.125 of 2007 corresponding to Dhanmondi Police Station Case No.20 of 2007 in which Mr. Anwar Hossain Monju has been tried as the principal offender and the respondent has been shown as abettor. The case of Anwar Hossain was split up and he has been convicted by the Special Judge. Thereupon, he preferred Criminal Appeal No. 3098 of 2009 in the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 10-8-2010 acquitted him of the charge. The Durnity Daman Commission thereupon preferred Leave Petition No.774 of 2012 before this Court. This court by judgment and order dated 15-11-2015 dismissed the leave petition. 

 3. The High Court Division quashed the proceedings on technical ground of lack, of proper sanction in the case and that there is no element of abatement against her even if the allegations in the FIR are taken to be true. Admittedly, the respondent absconded and at no point of time she appeared before the Special Judge. Though the respondent claimed that as no process was issued against her, she could not be said to be an absconder in the eye of law, it failed to notice that offences charged against the respondent are cognizable offences. At any event, since the principal offender has been acquitted of the charge, no fruitful purpose will be served if the respondent Tasmima Hossain is put on trial. However, this court has taken a consistent view that no writ petition is maintainable for quasninerit of a criminal proceeding and secondly, a fugitive from justice cannot get any relief from court. 

 4. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter. Therefore, we are of the view that the High Court Division has acted illegally in quashing the proceedings. Since the principal offender has been acquitted of the charge, if the respondent Tasmima Hossain appears and files an application for discharge, the Special Judge shall dispose of the matter in the light of the views taken by this court in Moyna Miah vs State, 1985 BLD (AD) 99 to the effect that after the acquittal or discharge of the principal offender, no fruitful purpose will be served if the trial of the case proceeds against the abettor. 

 5. Civil Petition No.1746 of 2008 has arisen out of Metropolitan Special Case No.122 of 2007 corresponding to Hazaribagh Police Station Case No.6 of 2007 dated 13-6-2007 and ACC GR Case No.45 of 2007. The High Court Division quashed the proceedings pursuant to a writ petition on the reasoning that no notice was served upon her under sections 26 or 27 of the Durnity Daman Commission. Ain, There is allegation that in connivance with her husband, late Md. Nasir Uddin Ahmed (Pintu), she has acquired property disproportionate to the known-sources of income. It is now settled that the offences under sections 26 and 27 of the Ain are distinct and that for initiation of a proceeding under section 27, no notice is required to be served. 

 6. More so, the respondent was a fugitive from justice at the time of making the petition and she challenged the proceedings by filing a writ-petition. The writ petition itself is misconceived one in presence of alternative remedy available, under the law. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. The trial of the case be proceeded against in accordance with law. 

 7. Civil Petition No.1776 of 2008 has arisen of ACC GR Case No. 165 of 2007 corresponding Gulshan PS Case No.47 of 2007, in which, the investigating agency submitted charge sheet against the respondent Shama Schezene Khan wife of Faisal Morshed Khan and her husband Faisal Morshed Khan. The case has given rise to Metro Sessions Case No.89 of 2008. 

 9. Writ petitioner Shama Schezene Khan had absconded and at no point of time, she appeared before the Special Judge. She also filed the writ petition challenging the proceedings of the case. The writ petition itself is a "misconceived one and that she being a fugitive from justice is not entitled to get any relief. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. 

 10. Civil Petition No. 1785 of 2008 has arisen out of ACR GR Case No. 86 of 2007 corresponding to Ramna Police Station Case No. 40 of 2007 and Metro Sessions Case No. 84 of 2008. The case was filed against the writ petitioner Md. Shamim Islam son of Nurul Islam Babul, Nurul Islam Babul and Ms Salma Islam. The writ petitioner has been arraigned as the principal offender. It is contended on behalf of the petitioner that the proceedings against Nurul Islam, Babul and Ms Salma Islam have been quashed by the High Court Division in a writ petition, and therefore, the proceeding against the writ petitioner are not legally maintainable. The writ petitioner absconded throughout the period of proceedings and his trial is still pending. The writ petition itself is misconceived one since this court has settled this point and that he being a fugitive from justice is not legally entitled to any relief from the court. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. 

 11. Civil Petition No. 1 786 of 2008 has arisen out of ACC GR Case No.73 of 2007 corresponding to Badda Police Station Case No. 5 of 2007. The case was initiated under sections 26 and 27 of the Durnity Daman Commission Ain. The writ petition itself is a misconceived one, inasmuch as, the writ petitioner has alternative remedy and that she was also fugitive from justice and therefore, not legally entitled to any relief from the court. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. 

 12. Civil Petition No.1787 of 2008 has arisen out of ACC GR Case No. 105 of 2007 corresponding to Ramna Police Station Case No.66 (9) of 2007. The case has been instituted against the writ petitioner and her husband Kamal Ahmed MajuMd.er for possession of wealth beyond their known sources of income. The writ petitioner Shahida Kamal was fugitive from justice, and therefore, she is not entitled to get any relief. More so, judicial review is not available for quashing a criminal proceeding in presence of alternative remedy. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. 

 13. Civil Petition No. 1778 of 2008 has arisen out of ACC GR Case No.31 of 2007 corresponding to Adabor Police Station Case No.17 of 2007. The High Court Division has quashed the proceedings in failing to consider that the writ petition is misconceived one More so, the trial of Ruhul Quddus Talukder Dulu, the principal offender of the case is pending before the Special Judge. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. 

 14. Civil Petition No. 1777 of 2008 has arisen out of ACC GR Case No. 164 of 2007 corresponding to Gulshan Police Station Case No.46 of 2007. This case stands on the same footing as in other cases. The writ petitioner Nasreen Khan had absconded and she made the petition without appearing before the trial court. More so, in presence of alternative remedy she moved the High Court Division a writ petition which is not maintainable in view of the views taken by this court. 

 15. It is contended that the writ petitioner's husband M Morshed Khan preferred Criminal Appeal No.3099 of 2009 against the judgment of the Special Judge in Special Case No. 21 of 2008 and the High Court Division has acquitted him of the charge. In view of the above, since the principal offender has been acquitted, no fruitful purpose will be served if the proceedings continue against the writ petitioner. 

 16. This court has consistently held that a fugitive from justice is not entitled to any relief from any court of law. All writ petitioners had absconded before they moved the High Court Division. There is no positive statement as to whether they appeared before the Special Judge before moving the petitions. This court further held that in presence of alternative remedy, a writ petition for quashing the proceeding is not maintainable. This court cannot take different view. The accused if feel aggrieved by the initiation of the proceedings, must surrender to the jurisdiction of the court before seeking any remedy. The court can exercise its jurisdiction in appropriate case if it is found that the proceedings have been initiated illegally or that the FIR and the police report do not disclose any offence or that the proceedings are abuse of the process of the court, inasmuch as, they have been initiated with oblique motive with a view to humiliate them. 

 17. We want to make it clear that in some cases the principal offenders have been acquitted of the charge from the appellate forum and the proceedings against the abettor who are none but their spouse and children are pending. After acquittal of the principal offender no proceedings against the abettor is maintainable. Reference in this connection is the case of Moyna Miah vs State, 1985 BLD (AD) 99. Despite such view, we are interfering with the judgment of the High Court Division merely on the ground that the writ petitions filed by the accused are not maintainable and that they did not surrender before the court below prior to the making of the petitions. If those accused make proper applications for discharge, the Special Judge shall consider their petition I sympathetically. The judgments of the High Court Division are set aside. The appeal and the petitions are disposed of with the above observations.
